title: Activation runbook & stability collab workplan — Q1 2027
body:
Purpose:
This is a pragmatic, cross-functional activation runbook to take the stability/dependability program from engineering pilots to org-wide enforcement for Q1 2027. It focuses on a lightweight SLO phasing approach, clear handoffs, and minimally-invasive tooling changes so product teams can adopt without major rewrites.

Background/context (short):
- Last 6 months: multiple pilot services adopted error-budget based alerts and prefixed caching; pilot results show ~15% cost saving and 30% fewer P1 escalations for pilot teams.
- Problem now: inconsistent SLO definitions across product areas, duplicated alerting, and unclear ownership for rollback/fallback policies. Need a repeatable activation playbook.

Scope (what this doc covers):
- Pilot -> Phase 1 (alpha) -> Phase 2 (beta) rollout plan for 6 product services
- Canonical SLO definitions, alerting thresholds, and error budget policy templates
- Cross-team roles + stakeholder map + meeting cadence
- Minimal tool changes (alert templates, dashboards, tracing tags) and required infra tickets

Out-of-scope (for now):
- Full automation of SLO enforcement (policy engine) — future work
- Overhauls of model-serving runtime (only config tweaks)

Goals / Success criteria (Q1 2027):
- 6 non-pilot services onboarded to canonical SLOs by end of Q1
- Observability templates in console for per-route latency and cost view
- 80% of incidents show improved MTTR within 3 months of onboarding
- Team owners able to run error-budget driven runbooks without SRE heavy lift

Proposed canonical SLO bundles (baseline):
- Availability SLO: request success rate >= 99.9% (rolling 30d)
- Latency SLOs: P95 <= 300ms for frontend-critical routes; P99 <= 1s for async batch endpoints
- Quality guardrail: end-to-end semantic accuracy regressions monitored via nightly evals (not an SLA but a signal)
- Error budget policy: consume alarm at 50% (informational), 75% (ops sync), 90% (rollback/fallback enablement)

Key stakeholders / RACI (short):
- R: Service Owner (product engineer on team)
- A: SRE Program Lead (Aisha Patel)
- C: Platform (Jordan Kim) — dashboards, tagging, runbook templates
- I: Product Manager / Solutions Eng (Sofia Martinez) — customer impact decisions
- Support escalation: oncall SRE then product oncall

Phased rollout plan (high level):
- Pilot (Nov 2026) — 2 services (completed)
- Phase 1 / Alpha (Dec 2026 - Jan 2027) — onboard 2 additional teams (low-risk services)
- Phase 2 / Beta (Feb 2027 - Mar 2027) — remaining 4 services, org-wide material change requests
- Post-rollout (Apr 2027) — retrospective, policy tweaks, automation backlog prioritization

Sprint-level milestones (first 12 weeks):
- Week 1 (kickoff): stakeholder map, finalize SLO templates, allocate tickets (owner assignment)
- Week 2-3: infra work — tracing/tagging + dashboard template landed (PLAT-2103)
- Week 4-5: team onboarding sessions (walkthrough + runbook rehearsals)
- Week 6: pilot alpha validation (observability smoke tests, golden signals)
- Week 7-10: phased activation and monitoring window
- Week 11-12: org retrospective + decision on enforcement automation backlog

Deliverables (concrete):
- SLO template doc (markdown) with examples per service type
- Alerting policy templates for PagerDuty and console alerts
- Dashboard bundle (latency/cost/error budget) + saved queries
- Onboarding checklist and runbook playbook for each service owner

Immediate infra tickets (must exist before alpha):
- PLAT-2103: add standardized "service.route" tracing tag to request paths (priority: high)
- SRE-1427: dashboard seed + alert rule templates (owner: Jordan)
- PROD-3189: gating rollback/fallback flagging in config service (owner: infra)

Meetings and cadence (recommended):
- Weekly activation sync (30m) — Aisha + platform lead + onboarding teams (Mon 9am)
- Bi-weekly stakeholder checkpoint (45m) — exec sponsors and PMs
- Ad-hoc war-room if error budget >90% (triggered by alert)

Onboarding checklist (short):
- [ ] Confirm team service owner and oncall
- [ ] Apply tracing tag + verify spans
- [ ] Deploy dashboard seed and validate metrics for 7 days
- [ ] Run simulated traffic test to exercise P95/P99 buckets
- [ ] Agree on rollback/fallback triggers and pre-approved actions
- [ ] Sign-off: product + SRE review (document results)

Runbook snippets (examples):
- If error_budget >75% for 24h: notify stakeholders, pause non-critical deployments, run synthetic tests, increase tracing sample rate
- If error_budget >90%: enable fallback mode (config flag), escalate to SRE exec, initiate postmortem if incident persists >1h

Risk register (top items):
- Risk: teams perceive SLOs as policing, leading to resistance. Mitigation: emphasize error budgets as product tools; run 1:1 sessions with PMs and show cost/quality tradeoffs.
- Risk: telemetry gaps cause false positives. Mitigation: mandatory tracing tags and 7-day validation window pre-activation.
- Risk: surge in operational overhead for small teams. Mitigation: platform-provided runbooks and opt-in managed activation for first month.

Open questions / decisions needed (TBD):
- Should we standardize to a single latency bucket set (P95/P99) for all services or allow per-service tailoring? (proposal: standardize for first 6 months, revisit.)
- Enforcement policy: opt-in for Q1, soft enforcement (advisory) thereafter — need exec signoff by Dec 10.

Notes to self / meeting artifacts: 
- Slack channel: #sre-dependability-activation (create if missing)
- Draft Confluence: CONFLUENCE-IDS/DEP-activation-2027 (link above)
- Pull requests to watch: infra PR linked above; once merged, schedule platform deploy window

Immediate next actions (this week):
- Aisha: finalize SLO examples and circulate to pilot owners (due Wed)
- Jordan: branch dashboard template and PR (due Fri)
- Sofia: prep customer-impact FAQ and PM talking points (due Fri)
- Ravi: create the GCP infra ticket for tracing sampling config (SRE-1427 subtask)

Appendix (useful references):
- Example SLO matrix (service-type -> availability/latency targets) — see attached table in Confluence
- Example alert threshold tuning notes from pilot run (internal notes)

Style/tone note: keep this lightweight and iterative — this doc should be the single source for the team running the Q1 activation. Expect to iterate heavily after alpha.
